title: News Aggregator
description: Build a news aggregator that stores articles, filters by category and source, sorts by date, and renders a headline list.

steps.title: Define the article data structure
steps.description: Create an `articles` array with objects containing `title`, `source`, `category`, `date` (ISO string), and `url`. Populate with at least 5 sample articles and log them.
hints: Article: { title: '...', source: 'BBC News', category: 'technology', date: '2025-01-15', url: '...' }
Use various categories: technology, sports, business, science, health
Use JSON.stringify to log the articles array

codeTemplate.python:
import json

articles = [
  {"title": "AI Breakthrough Announced", "source": "TechCrunch", "category": "technology", "date": "2025-01-15", "url": "https://example.com/ai"},
  {"title": "Championship Final Results", "source": "ESPN", "category": "sports", "date": "2025-01-14", "url": "https://example.com/sports"},
  {"title": "Stock Market Hits New High", "source": "Bloomberg", "category": "business", "date": "2025-01-16", "url": "https://example.com/stocks"},
  {"title": "Mars Rover Finds Water", "source": "NASA", "category": "science", "date": "2025-01-13", "url": "https://example.com/mars"},
  {"title": "New Vaccine Shows Promise", "source": "WebMD", "category": "health", "date": "2025-01-15", "url": "https://example.com/vaccine"}
]

print("Articles:", len(articles))
print(json.dumps(articles[0]))

verification.successMessage: Article data structure is set up with 5 articles across different categories!
verification.failureMessage: Create an articles array with at least 5 articles, each having title, source, category, date, and url.

steps.title: Filter articles by category
steps.description: Write a `filterByCategory` function that takes a `category` string and returns articles matching that category. Log the filtered results for `"technology"`.
hints: Return the filtered array (does not modify the original)
Log the count of matching articles and their titles

verification.test: output.includes('Tech articles: 2') && output.includes('AI Breakthrough') && output.includes('New Phone')
verification.successMessage: Articles can be filtered by category correctly!
verification.failureMessage: filterByCategory('technology') should return 2 articles: 'AI Breakthrough' and 'New Phone Release'.

steps.title: Filter articles by source
steps.description: Write a `filterBySource` function that takes a `source` string and returns articles from that source. Log the results for `"ESPN"`.
hints: Case-sensitive or case-insensitive matching is fine
Log the matching articles' titles and dates

verification.test: output.includes('ESPN articles: 2') && output.includes('Sports Update') && output.includes('Game Highlights')
verification.successMessage: Articles can be filtered by source!
verification.failureMessage: filterBySource('ESPN') should return 2 articles: 'Sports Update' and 'Game Highlights'.

steps.title: Sort articles by date (newest first)
steps.description: Write a `sortByDate` function that returns a new array sorted by date in descending order (newest first). Log the sorted article titles with dates.
hints: Compare dates: new Date(b.date) - new Date(a.date) or string comparison
Log each article's title and date after sorting

verification.successMessage: Articles sort by date with newest first!
verification.failureMessage: sortByDate should return articles ordered: 'Recent News' (Jan 15), 'Middle News' (Jan 12), 'Old News' (Jan 10).

steps.title: Combine filtering and sorting
steps.description: Write a `getArticles` function that takes optional `category` and `source` parameters, filters accordingly, then sorts by date. Return the filtered + sorted array.
hints: Start with a copy of articles: let result = [...articles]
If category is provided, filter by it; same for source
Sort the result by date descending before returning

verification.successMessage: Combined filtering and sorting returns the correct subset in order!
verification.failureMessage: getArticles('technology', 'TechCrunch') should return 'AI News' (Jan 15) then 'Tech Today' (Jan 14).

steps.title: Render the headline list
steps.description: Write a `renderHeadlines` function that takes an array of articles and returns a formatted string with numbered headlines: `"1. AI Breakthrough (TechCrunch - Jan 15)"`. Log the result.
hints: Use .map() to format each article with its index + 1
Join with newlines for the final string

verification.successMessage: Headlines render with numbering and source attribution!
verification.failureMessage: renderHeadlines should format as '1. AI Breakthrough (TechCrunch - 2025-01-15)\n2. Sports Update (ESPN - 2025-01-14)'.
